nc_breakfast_wall.blurb: Breakfast Wall is the first big cliff you meet in the West Walls, the gentler western section of the Cooks Wall climbing at Hanging Rock State Park. Eleven routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a handful of trad, on quartzite. Grades run from the mid 5.6 range up to low 5.12, but most lines sit at 5.10 and harder, so it suits climbers who already lead the middle grades. The face is built around an eye-catching arete, with routes on its front and right side; the right-hand lines begin high in a gully above a ledge. Expect a quiet, wooded setting.
nc_breakfast_wall.approach: Take the Cooks Wall trail across the top of the cliff, then keep going into the woods and drop left down a steep slope with a rocky ridge on your right. Breakfast Wall is the first large wall reached.

nc_holloway_mountain.blurb: Holloway Mountain is a short, easy-access cliff above Foscoe, a few minutes from Boone in the Northern Mountains. Eleven climbs, nearly all trad cracks, plus one bolted line and one top-rope problem. Grades start very easy and reach the low 5.12s, though most lines fall between 5.6 and 5.9, which makes it a friendly place for newer climbers learning gear and top-rope setups. The cliff picks up afternoon sun, so it stays usable through much of the year. Summer weekends can be busy and student groups often work the right side, so weekdays are quieter.
